conventions: Labels judge what the student SAID, applying each item's label and guidance literally; information the patient volunteered without being asked does not earn an 'Asks…' item.
Half-credit items (introduce-first-year, share-assessment) are labelled 1 only for full performance; the partial version is recorded under 'half'.
sh-sexual: not relevant to this presentation, so omission scores 1. sh-travel: relevant (pulmonary embolism is on the expected differential), so omission scores 0 and is marked borderline.

ROS items need a question about a symptom of that system beyond exploring the chief concern itself (e.g. pulmonary = cough/wheeze/sputum; cardiac = chest pain/palpitations/leg swelling; neuro = dizziness/fainting/numbness/weakness). Emotional-context questions are not psychiatric ROS.

elicit-preferences needs the patient's views/concerns about the plan; a generic 'Any (other) questions?' alone scores 0 (borderline). teach-back needs more than 'Does that make sense?' (borderline). transition-pe needs both the announcement and a request for permission.

prioritize follows the guidance literally: with a single concern it scores 1 only when the student explicitly confirmed there was nothing else; note-issues scores 0 when no additional issue was raised (borderline).
